chunks: Jarrah al-Madā'inī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “How is the salutation upon the people of the graves?” So he said:

“You stand and say: Peace be upon the inhabitants of the abodes from among the believers and the Muslims. May Allah have mercy on those who have gone before us and those who come later, and indeed, if Allah wills, we shall join you.”

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْقُبُورِ: the inhabitants of the graves, meaning the deceased
key_terms.التَّسْلِيمُ: the act of offering salutation or greeting
key_terms.السَّلَامُ: peace; the greeting invoked upon others
key_terms.الْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ: those who have gone ahead earlier
key_terms.لَاحِقُونَ: those who will follow or join later

ai.seo_question: How should one greet the inhabitants of the graves according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the wording for offering salām to the inhabitants of the graves when visiting them. It combines greeting, mercy, and remembrance of death, affirming that the living will eventually join the deceased by the will of Allah.
